stories.title: A Heart Attack Without a Severely Blocked Artery? Why This Matters, Especially for Women
stories.description: A new international definition of myocardial infarction, developed by four major cardiac organisations, aims to simplify how heart attacks are classified by focusing on their underlying cause rather than complex numerical categories. The updated system groups heart attacks into three broad types: those caused by an acute coronary artery problem, those triggered by an imbalance between the heart’s oxygen supply and demand, and those linked to a recent cardiac procedure or surgery. Experts say the change could help doctors provide more individualised care, particularly for women, who may experience heart attacks linked to conditions such as spontaneous coronary artery dissection or coronary artery spasm that do not always involve a severely blocked artery. They also stress that women should not wait for the classic crushing chest pain, as symptoms can include breathlessness, unexplained severe fatigue, nausea, sweating, dizziness and pain or discomfort in the jaw, back, shoulder or arm. While the new definition is an important step, experts say its benefits will depend on how consistently it is adopted and understood by both healthcare professionals and patients.

stories.title: Long-term cardiorenal illness trajectories after initiation of antihypertensive medications in adults with and without ADHD: a nationwide cohort study
stories.description: Adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) have a higher prevalence and incidence of hypertension, but whether long-term cardiorenal trajectories after the initiation of antihypertensive medications differ by ADHD status is unclear. Here, in this nationwide retrospective cohort study using Dutch register data, we included 706,414 new users (52.2% female, aged 18–90 years) of antihypertensive medications without prior cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease (CKD); 10,689 had ADHD. Multistate modelling was used to characterize long-term cardiorenal illness trajectories and compare transition-specific rates between adults with and without ADHD. Adults with ADHD had higher adjusted rates of heart failure hospitalization (HHF; hazard ratio (HR), 1.46; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.12–1.90) and stroke (HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.03–1.38) after antihypertensive medication initiation. They also had higher adjusted rates of cardiorenal death after HHF (HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.01–3.17) or CKD (HR, 2.57; 95% CI, 1.33–4.97) onset. Ten-year trajectories through HHF or CKD to cardiorenal death were more common in adults with ADHD. This research investigates long-term cardiorenal outcomes in adults initiating antihypertensive medications, revealing that those with ADHD experience significantly higher rates of heart failure hospitalization, stroke and cardiorenal death than counterparts without ADHD, using multistate modelling for analysis.

stories.title: Genomic insights into fossorial transition, hibernation, and hypoxia adaptation in ground squirrels
stories.description: The evolutionary shift from arboreal to fossorial lifestyles, coupled with deep hibernation and high-altitude hypoxia tolerance, represents a suite of extreme physiological adaptations unique to ground squirrels. To investigate the molecular basis of these interconnected traits, we generated a chromosome-level genome of the Himalayan marmot (Marmota himalayana) and conducted comparative analyses across 11 squirrel species. Evolutionary breakpoint regions distinguishing arboreal from fossorial taxa were enriched in bone morphogenesis and motor nervous system genes, providing testable hypotheses for the fossorial transition. Positively selected genes in hibernating ground squirrels included circadian regulators, and a hibernator-specific TIMELESS Leu173Phe mutation enhanced PER2 binding in co-immunoprecipitation assays, offering a candidate mechanism for circadian dampening during torpor. In M. himalayana, a fixed EPAS1 Thr478Met variant reduced protein expression under hypoxia while upregulating LDHA and VEGF, revealing a fine-tuned strategy for high-altitude adaptation. Together, these findings provide molecular insights into three key evolutionary innovations with TIMELESS and EPAS1 variants are supported by functional validations and the fossorial transition representing comparative genomic hypotheses awaiting further testing. The authors sequence the Himalayan marmot genome and compare 11 squirrel species, revealing candidate genes underlying fossorial transition, a hibernator-specific TIMELESS mutation enhancing PER2 binding, and an EPAS1 variant tuning hypoxia adaptation.

stories.title: The New Lobster Upgrade Is Here
stories.description: This cutting-edge graph neural network architecture, **Faster than GAT 6**, achieves 6x higher inference and training speed than standard Graph Attention Networks (GAT) while preserving 99% of state-of-the-art prediction accuracy across node classification, link prediction and graph-level analysis tasks. Optimized with sparse attention pruning, dynamic feature caching and batch-friendly graph sampling mechanisms, it eliminates the redundant computational overhead of vanilla multi-head self-attention on large-scale graph datasets, delivering ultra-efficient performance for real-time graph analytics scenarios including social network mining, e-commerce recommendation systems, financial fraud detection and biomedical molecular property prediction. As a high-performance upgraded alternative to traditional GAT frameworks, it breaks through the long-existing efficiency bottleneck of attention-based graph models, providing a scalable deployment solution for industrial-level large graph processing without compromising task performance.
